title: Hang the jumper or lay it flat?
hook: A wet jumper holds about 0.6 kg. Pegged at two points, how much does each point carry?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that pegging a wet knit at two points puts all its water weight on those points, which can stretch it, while drying it flat spreads the weight, and many knit care labels say dry flat

misconception: Hanging a wet jumper on a line is fine, because its weight is the same however it is held.
objective: In an ideal equal-share model, more support points reduce the load assigned to each. A garment’s care label can require flat drying; this drawing explains support sharing without predicting fabric stretch.

recall.question: A wet sweater weighs 900 g. In the ideal equal-share model, how much does each point carry with 2 support points, and with 6?
recall.why: Equal sharing divides the load: 900 ÷ 2 = 450 g, and 900 ÷ 6 = 150 g. The model does not predict stretch; if the label says dry flat, follow the label.
